steps.prompt: Think of a friend or family member. What is one thing they always say, or one way they always talk?

cards.title: Voice
cards.body: Every person talks a little differently. Some use long words, some use short ones. Some joke, some complain, some ask lots of questions. In a story, the way a character talks shows who they are.

cards.title: Same problem, two voices
cards.text: "Um, I think maybe we're lost? Sorry. I mean, it's okay if we are." / "Lost? Us? Nah. We're exploring. Follow me!"
cards.note: You can tell these are two different people without any names. One is nervous and polite. The other is bold and sure of themselves.

cards.title: Speech habits
cards.body: A speech habit is something a character says or does when they talk: a favourite word ("Seriously?"), always asking questions, never finishing sentences, or speaking very formally. One habit, used a few times, makes a character easy to recognise.

cards.title: Spot the habit
cards.prompt: Tap the word Zara keeps repeating. It's her speech habit.
cards.text: "Best day ever, literally," Zara said. "The pool was literally freezing, and Mom literally screamed."

cards.title: Punctuating speech
cards.body: Put the spoken words inside quotation marks, and start a new paragraph each time a different person speaks. That way readers always know who is talking.

prompts: What speech habit did you give one of your characters? What does it show about them?
Read your dialogue out loud. Do your two characters sound different?
